why: Both concern reactions to the sub's own April Fools styling, but one objects to the jokes while the other works around or switches off the look.

why.T3-142: The item's concepts are ethnic and national insults aimed at Croatian attackers during a canvas fight, matching T3-142 rather than mere taunting or defence.

why.T3-004: The concepts work out the belt's look and details: colour, arrow spacing, direction, curves, corners, underground sections, and corrections against a reference.

why.T3-159: The clearest placed practice is rewarding helpers: offering a printed version of the work to people who helped the flag, a prize/giveaway for the room's helpers.

why.T3-032: Many concepts object to the sub's April Fools joke as unfunny, tiring, or unwanted and ask for it to stop.
why.T3-097: Several concepts treat the prank styling as something to get past: turning off custom themes, waiting for CSS to change back, and repairing navigation blocked by the layout.
why.T3-100: Some concepts ask to keep April Fools flair changes after the day, including wanting flairs back or keeping a shiny flair forever.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-032 covers objections to the jokes but does not carry the acts of turning off the custom theme or repairing navigation blocked by the prank layout.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0531080 shows how to uncheck custom themes and C0025041 asks to fix the Facebook link, satisfying T3-097's gate with distinct support.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-097 if forced to one; would lose the workaround/switch-off side of the prank reaction.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-032 covers objections but not the wish to keep April Fools flairs after the event.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0444134 accepts keeping the shiny Malcolm flair forever and C0846321 wants the special flair again, satisfying T3-100's gate with distinct support.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-100 if forced to one; would lose the keep-the-flair request.

why.T3-068: The concepts report changing Homestuck's logo into Homelab's sign, turning another room's art into the room's own mark.

why.T3-031: The exchange plays the room's own Old Bird running joke and meets a literal admission of unfamiliarity, matching the in-joke theme.

why.T3-149: The concepts discuss and reject a peace offer and redirect peace talks to an ally, matching truce/peace negotiation with rival rooms.

why.T3-001: The concepts are the room's own April Fools fakes, teasers, leaks, edits, rickrolls, and later reveals, staged as if true and then exposed.

why.T3-023: The sub is turned into a mock GameSpot/CBS universe for April Fools, announced by the moderators and played inside with corporate fiction and posts.

why.T3-020: The concepts are about where Baby Groot should go: above Daft Punk, inside the EU flag, below the void, or on rainbow road.

why.T3-028: Two concepts concern bot/script use for pixel work: asking for code against a suspected bot and reporting bots maintaining logos.
why.T3-014: One concept considers starting a Discord to recruit people, moving coordination into a chat.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-028 covers the bot/script element but does not carry the proposal to start a Discord for recruiting.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0327467 considers starting a Discord to recruit people, satisfying T3-014's chat-coordination gate with distinct support.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-014 if forced to one; would lose the Discord-recruiting element.

why.T3-168: The central practice is making the Rust bot/script coexist with neighboring art by changing targets, leaving squares untouched, and asking for script edits to spare neighbours.

why.T3-031: The more-jpeg bot trigger and explanation are an in-room running joke exchange rather than canvas scripting for the work.

why.T3-028: The concepts share, run, justify, and thank scripts/bots used to auto-paint and keep the PoE logo repaired.

why.T3-006: The concepts call for, carry out, celebrate, or recount attacks that wreck TSM marks, matching defacement of rivals' work.
